root_cause.text: In the FUSE synchronous INIT path, the kernel treated the mount thread’s `FUSE_INIT` request as non-abortable and kept `FR_FORCE` set, so a fatal signal or server crash during init could not trigger `fuse_abort_conn()` while the mounting thread still held the device fd open, causing the mount to hang.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `abort_on_kill` to `struct fuse_args`, sets it in `fuse_send_init()` only for `fm->fc->sync_init`, and changes `request_wait_answer()` to call `fuse_abort_conn(fc)` when `args->abort_on_kill` is set; it also stops setting `FR_FORCE` for such requests, matching the CVE text that the mount thread “will keep the device fd open, which will prevent an abort from happening.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Abort the FUSE connection when a kill-interrupted request is marked abort_on_kill.
intent_record.what: In request_wait_answer(), a new conditional block was added after a nonzero error check: if req->args->abort_on_kill is set, the code now calls fuse_abort_conn(fc) and returns immediately before the existing FR_URING pending-request removal path.
intent_record.how: When a request wait is interrupted and the request is marked abort_on_kill, the connection is now aborted outright instead of continuing through the normal cleanup/removal logic. This changes runtime behavior to terminate the FUSE connection on kill-related interruption for those requests.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid force-marking abort-on-kill FUSE requests so they can be interrupted and aborted correctly.
intent_record.what: In __fuse_simple_request(), the unconditional setting of the FR_FORCE bit on req->flags was replaced with a conditional check so that FR_FORCE is only set when args->abort_on_kill is false; the FR_WAITING bit assignment remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: This changes request handling so that requests marked abort_on_kill are no longer forced to continue waiting or bypass normal interruption behavior, while all other requests still retain the previous forced-wait semantics.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an `abort_on_kill` flag to `struct fuse_args` so FUSE request handling can represent kill-triggered abort behavior.
intent_record.what: A new one-bit boolean field named `abort_on_kill` was added to `struct fuse_args` immediately after `invalidate_vmap`.
intent_record.how: This change expands the `fuse_args` structure to carry an additional state flag, allowing code that builds or consumes these arguments to mark a request for abort behavior when a kill condition occurs. By itself, the hunk does not alter control flow, but it enables later logic to distinguish this case at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark synchronous FUSE init requests as abortable on kill so initialization requests are canceled correctly.
intent_record.what: In `fuse_send_init(struct fuse_mount *fm)`, when `fm->fc->sync_init` is true, the code now sets `ia->args.abort_on_kill = true` immediately before calling `fuse_simple_request(fm, &ia->args)`.
intent_record.how: This causes the synchronous FUSE init request to be aborted if the request is killed, rather than continuing to wait or complete normally, changing the request handling behavior during initialization.

grouping_result.intent: Mark synchronous FUSE init requests as abortable on kill so initialization requests are canceled correctly.
Avoid force-marking abort-on-kill FUSE requests so they can be interrupted and aborted correctly.
Add an `abort_on_kill` flag to `struct fuse_args` so FUSE request handling can represent kill-triggered abort behavior.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: the synchronous FUSE INIT request was previously treated as non-abortable, preventing connection abort on fatal signal or crash. Marking these init requests abortable on kill and aborting the connection when such a request is interrupted addresses the mount-hang condition.
The change directly matches the root cause: it removes force-marking of abort-on-kill FUSE requests so the synchronous INIT request can be interrupted/aborted instead of hanging during mount.

The root cause is that the synchronous FUSE INIT path was not treated as abortable on fatal signal/server failure, which prevented connection abort during mount. Adding an `abort_on_kill` flag directly addresses kill-triggered abort behavior in FUSE request handling and is aligned with fixing that issue.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable synchronous-init hang condition is not present in this commit’s code. The key fix is visible in `fuse_send_init()`: for synchronous init (`if (fm->fc->sync_init)`), it now uses `err = fuse_simple_request(fm, &ia->args);` instead of the old always-background path, and then normalizes the reply (`if (err > 0) err = 0;`). Crucially, the old asynchronous-only logic that forced the request and relied on background completion (`ia->args.end = process_init_reply; ... fuse_simple_background(...)`) is now only used in the non-sync path. Also, `fuse_fill_super_common()` recognizes `FUSE_DEV_SYNC_INIT` and sets `fc->sync_init = 1`, which enables the new synchronous handling. Since the root cause was that the mount thread’s `FUSE_INIT` was treated as non-abortable with `FR_FORCE` kept set, this code already contains the corrected synchronous path rather than the buggy behavior.
